exemplars.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Enhance Domain Expert Inclusion in Data Science Workflows
exemplars.why: Data scientists manipulate data in notebooks while domain experts receive a dedicated dashboard that translates the same tracked dataframe state into summaries and SnapGrid version cards, clearly demonstrating two role-specific surfaces connected through shared state.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above AACessTalk because the evidence explicitly identifies the separate interfaces, the shared state, and the transformation that carries one role’s actions into the other role’s view.

exemplars.title: AACessTalk: Fostering Communication between Minimally Verbal Autistic Children and Parents with Contextual Guidance and Card Recommendation
exemplars.why: Within one shared conversation, the parent receives real-time engagement guidance while the child receives contextual vocabulary cards, giving the two participants complementary role-specific assistance rather than a common interface.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above the hybrid Wizard-of-Oz system because its asymmetric channels directly support equitable participation between two end participants, making the pattern more consequential and less tied to prototyping infrastructure.

exemplars.title: Prototyping Multimodal GenAI Real-Time Agents with Counterfactual Replays and Hybrid Wizard-of-Oz
exemplars.why: The wizard privately triggers model operations and chooses whether generated messages cross into the user’s separate SocraBot interface, exposing both the role-gated control channel and the controlled propagation of shared interaction state.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Accompany Sleep because the evidence explicitly establishes a private operator surface and selective cross-view state transition, whereas the parent-app and child-projector quote does not establish that either channel is private.

notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order; no system_id is repeated. Scores were adjusted only slightly, so no adjustment exceeds 0.3. AACessTalk’s evidence should be treated with some caution because it establishes role-targeted outputs but does not explicitly say that they appear in separate applications or that the parent guidance is private. The Wizard-of-Oz exemplar is structurally strong, but its operator–user asymmetry is a familiar research-prototyping arrangement and may generalize less directly to deployed multi-party products. The first exemplar has the most complete structural evidence, although its quote describes tracked notebook changes flowing toward the expert dashboard more clearly than it describes state flowing in the reverse direction.
